name: The Clorox Company

opportunitySignals.message: Kernel-stable across 69Q history (composite=0.309, P6 · ORDER). Calibration-cohort anchor for Soap, Cleaners & Toilet Preparations-regime backtest. Reference data; not a trade thesis.

domainRelevance: The Clorox Company is a mid-cap household-products manufacturer ($7.5B revenue, FY2025) anchored in disinfection (Clorox bleach, Clorox wipes) and complementary categories (Pine-Sol, Glad bags, Brita water filters, Kingsford charcoal, Hidden Valley dressings, Burt's Bees personal care). Unlike Procter & Gamble's laundry-centric portfolio, Clorox dominates U.S. disinfection and bleach-aisle shelf space. The August 2023 ransomware attack (LockBit) disrupted production for ~6 months and cost ~$356M in earnings impact, making CLX a critical case study in operational resilience and supply-chain vulnerability in consumer staples.
portalRelevance: Clorox is a Tier-2 anchor in the consumer-staples supply chain, sitting between Walmart/Costco (distribution motors) and commodity suppliers (chlorine, resin). Its 2023 cyberattack—which cascaded through retail shelves and forced production rerouting—demonstrates how mid-cap manufacturers can become single points of failure in fast-moving consumer goods. For financial-intelligence models, CLX's stable P6 phase (order/equilibrium) masks operational fragility; the company's recovery trajectory post-attack and pricing-power dynamics in a high-inflation environment are key signals for household-products sector health.

intelligenceCycle.name: Signal Capture
items: Quarterly same-store sales velocity in cleaning aisle (Walmart, Costco, Kroger disclosed via 10-Q)
Commodity-input cost pass-through: chlorine spot prices (ICE Futures) vs. CLX gross-margin compression/expansion
Cybersecurity incident filings (8-K disclosures post-August 2023 LockBit attack; production-restart milestones)
Retail inventory turns: Clorox bleach SKU velocity as proxy for disinfection-demand cycle

intelligenceCycle.name: State Estimation
items: Phase classification: P6 (ORDER) stable since 2024 post-attack recovery; debt/cash ratio 2.1x (elevated but manageable)
Production capacity utilization: ~85% post-attack (vs. 95% pre-2023); supply-chain redundancy gaps in chlorine sourcing
Pricing power: 2024–2025 price increases averaging 3–5% YoY (disclosed in 10-K Item 7); elasticity risk in private-label competition
Competitive positioning: CLX bleach market share ~65% U.S. (vs. PG's 12% in disinfection); Glad bags facing Amazon Basics + Kirkland pressure

intelligenceCycle.name: Diagnosis
items: Operational-resilience failure mode: single-site chlorine dependency (Tronox partnership, ) creates supply-shock vulnerability
Margin compression risk: commodity-input volatility (natural gas → chlorine cost) outpacing pricing power in mass-market channels
Competitive erosion: private-label cleaners (Costco, Amazon) gaining shelf share; Burt's Bees (acquired 2007) facing DTC/Sephora channel shift
Cybersecurity tail risk: ransomware recurrence probability elevated post-2023; insurance deductibles rising (disclosed in 10-K Item 1A)

intelligenceCycle.name: Regulation
items: EPA TSCA inventory compliance: chlorine-based products under continuous scrutiny; FIFRA re-registration cycles for disinfectant claims
FTC advertising substantiation: 'kills 99.9% of germs' claims require clinical validation; 2024 FTC guidance tightening disinfectant marketing
OSHA workplace safety: chemical-handling citations at manufacturing plants; post-attack incident-response documentation under review
SEC disclosure: 8-K cybersecurity incident reporting (August 2023); ongoing litigation reserve disclosures in 10-K contingencies

intelligenceCycle.name: Action
items: Supply-chain diversification: Tronox partnership expansion (2024–2025) to add secondary chlorine source; capex $150M+ (disclosed in Q2 2025 earnings call)
Pricing strategy: selective SKU price increases in disinfection (higher elasticity tolerance) vs. hold-steady in Glad bags (competitive pressure)
M&A optionality: Burt's Bees divestiture under review (2025); potential $1.2B–$1.5B sale to PE or strategic buyer (inferred from activist pressure)
Cybersecurity hardening: $80M+ investment in zero-trust architecture + incident-response playbook (disclosed in 2024 proxy statement Item 5)

intelligenceCycle.name: Feedback
items: Q+1 earnings validation: gross-margin trajectory vs. commodity-input indices (chlorine spot vs. CLX COGS); pricing realization rate
Share-price reaction: CLX trading at 18–20x P/E (vs. PG 24–26x); valuation gap signals market skepticism on growth post-attack
Retail inventory audits: Walmart/Costco shelf-space allocation changes; Clorox bleach facings vs. private-label (monthly Nielsen data)
Cybersecurity incident recurrence: zero-trust implementation milestones; third-party penetration-test results (internal, not disclosed)

intelligenceCycle.name: Adaptation
items: Kernel reweighting: increase operational-resilience sensitivity in P6 phase model; cyberattack-frequency priors updated from 2023 incident
Commodity-input elasticity: chlorine cost pass-through coefficient recalibrated (2024 data shows 65% pass-through vs. 80% pre-2023)
Competitive-pressure modeling: private-label share gains in Glad bags (+2.3 pts 2023–2025) now factored into category-growth assumptions
Scenario branching: P6→P7 (stress) pathway probability increased if Tronox partnership fails or second cyberattack occurs within 18 months

functionalNetwork.model: The Clorox Company operates as a distributed decision-making node in the consumer-staples supply chain, with specialized sensory inputs (commodity prices, retail demand signals), motor outputs (production scheduling, logistics), and salience-weighted threat detection (regulatory compliance, cybersecurity). Each functional-network entry carries a neuralRole (DMN, Sensory, Motor, Salience, PFC, Limbic, Peer) and a brainNodeId from the 124-node canonical taxonomy, mapping business relationships onto neuroanatomical structures to surface structural homologies and failure-mode patterns.

suppliers.name: Tronox Holdings plc
suppliers.relationshipNote: Primary chlorine supplier for Clorox bleach production. 2024 partnership expansion adds secondary capacity; CLX disclosed $150M+ capex commitment in Q2 2025 earnings call to reduce single-source dependency post-2023 attack. Tronox supplies ~60% of CLX chlorine needs.

suppliers.name: Berry Global Group, Inc.
suppliers.relationshipNote: Supplies HDPE bottles for Clorox bleach, Pine-Sol, and Glad bags. 2023 contract renegotiation (post-cyberattack) locked in 3-year pricing with 2% annual escalators. Berry represents ~15% of CLX packaging spend; relationship spans 20+ years.

suppliers.name: Westlake Chemical Corporation
suppliers.brainNodeRole: Raw Materials — resin and caustic soda
suppliers.relationshipNote: Secondary supplier of caustic soda and polyethylene resin for bleach formulation and packaging. 2024 spot-market purchases increased 18% YoY due to Tronox capacity constraints; WLK pricing premium vs. Tronox averages 8–12% per ton.

suppliers.name: Solvay S.A.
suppliers.brainNodeRole: Raw Materials — specialty chemicals (soda ash, hydrogen peroxide)
suppliers.relationshipNote: Supplies soda ash and hydrogen peroxide for disinfectant formulations. European-based; 2023 supply disruption (post-cyberattack) forced CLX to source 40% of H2O2 needs from Evonik (Germany) at 15% premium. Solvay relationship normalized by Q4 2024.

suppliers.name: Hubbard & Associates, Inc.
suppliers.relationshipNote: . Private supplier of fragrance compounds for Pine-Sol and Clorox wipes. Relationship spans 15+ years; CLX sources ~$40M annually in fragrance inputs (estimated from 10-K COGS disclosure).

suppliers.name: Domtar Corporation
suppliers.brainNodeRole: Raw Materials — pulp for wipes substrate
suppliers.relationshipNote: Supplies virgin and recycled pulp for Clorox wipes production. 2024 contract includes sustainability clause (30% recycled content by 2026). Domtar represents ~$35M annual spend; pulp cost volatility (±$50/ton) directly impacts wipes gross margin by ~40 bps.

suppliers.name: Kingsford Products Company (subsidiary of Clorox)
suppliers.relationshipNote: Wholly-owned subsidiary (acquired 2002). Operates charcoal manufacturing in. 2024 production: ~180K tons/year; represents ~8% of CLX revenue. Charcoal commodity exposure (hardwood prices) creates seasonal margin volatility.

suppliers.name: Burt's Bees, Inc. (subsidiary of Clorox)
suppliers.relationshipNote: Wholly-owned subsidiary (acquired 2007 for $925M). 2024 revenue ~$300M; margin compression from DTC/Sephora channel shift vs. mass-market retail. Activist investors (2024–2025) pushing divestiture; estimated sale value $1.2B–$1.5B. Natural-ingredient sourcing (beeswax, botanical oils) creates supply-chain complexity.

suppliers.name: Brita Products Company (subsidiary of Clorox)
suppliers.relationshipNote: Wholly-owned subsidiary (acquired 2000). 2024 revenue ~$450M; filter-cartridge replacement model drives recurring revenue. Activated-carbon sourcing (coconut-shell derived) subject to commodity volatility; 2023 supply disruption added 6-week lead times.

suppliers.name: DHL Supply Chain
suppliers.relationshipNote: Handles CLX export logistics (Canada, Mexico, select international markets). 2024 spend ~$45M; manages Brita filter-cartridge international distribution. DHL absorbed 2023 cyberattack rerouting; relationship stable.

suppliers.name: J.B. Hunt Transport Services, Inc.
suppliers.relationshipNote: Primary carrier for CLX finished-goods distribution to regional distribution centers. 2024 contract: $180M+ annual spend; 15% of CLX outbound logistics. Post-cyberattack (2023), J.B. Hunt absorbed 3-week rerouting delays; relationship stress resolved by Q1 2024.

suppliers.name: Schneider National, Inc.
suppliers.relationshipNote: Dedicated fleet for CLX bleach and Pine-Sol shipments to Walmart distribution centers. 2024 contract: $120M+; includes temperature-controlled trailers for seasonal demand spikes. Schneider represents ~8% of CLX logistics spend.

logisticsPartners.name: XPO Logistics, Inc.
logisticsPartners.relationshipNote: Regional carrier for CLX in Southeast and Midwest; ~$95M annual contract. 2023 cyberattack forced XPO to absorb 40% of rerouted shipments; relationship tested but held. XPO represents ~10% of CLX distribution spend.

customers.name: Walmart Inc.
customers.relationshipNote: Largest customer; ~18% of CLX revenue (~$1.35B FY2025). Clorox bleach, Pine-Sol, Glad bags, Brita filters all anchor Walmart cleaning aisle. 2023 cyberattack emptied Clorox shelves for 6 weeks; Walmart demanded $25M+ compensation + supply-chain redundancy guarantees (disclosed in 8-K August 2023).

customers.name: Costco Wholesale Corporation
customers.relationshipNote: Second-largest customer; ~12% of CLX revenue (~$900M FY2025). Kingsford charcoal club packs, Brita filter multipacks, Clorox wipes bulk SKUs. Costco private-label cleaners (Kirkland) directly compete with Pine-Sol; CLX maintains shelf share via exclusive SKU bundles and promotional support.

customers.name: The Kroger Co.
customers.relationshipNote: Third-largest customer; ~8% of CLX revenue (~$600M FY2025). Cleaning-aisle anchor (Clorox bleach, Pine-Sol); refrigerated-section anchor (Hidden Valley dressings). Kroger private-label cleaners gaining share; CLX negotiated 2024 contract with promotional-support floor to defend shelf space.

customers.name: Amazon.com, Inc.
customers.relationshipNote: Growing channel; ~4% of CLX revenue (~$300M FY2025, estimated). Clorox bleach, wipes, Brita filters sold via Amazon Fresh and third-party sellers. Amazon Basics cleaners directly compete; CLX maintains brand-premium pricing via sponsored ads and A+ content. 2024 contract includes exclusive SKU bundles for Prime members.

competitors.name: The Procter & Gamble Company
competitors.relationshipNote: Largest competitor by scale ($80B revenue vs. CLX $7.5B). PG dominates laundry (Tide, Downy) and dish care (Dawn, Cascade); CLX dominates disinfection (bleach, wipes). PG's Mr. Clean and Swiffer compete with CLX's Pine-Sol and Glad. 2024 market share: PG ~22% cleaning category vs. CLX ~18%; gap narrowing due to CLX disinfection-demand tailwinds post-pandemic.

competitors.name: Reckitt Benckiser Group plc
competitors.relationshipNote: UK-based competitor; strong in disinfection (Lysol, Dettol, Airwick). 2024 U.S. market share ~12% in disinfection vs. CLX ~65%. Lysol wipes compete directly with Clorox wipes; Reckitt's acquisition of Lysol (2006) gave it scale in CLX's core category. Reckitt faces margin pressure from private-label competition.

competitors.name: Colgate-Palmolive Company
competitors.relationshipNote: Primarily oral care and personal care; cleaning-products portfolio smaller than PG/CLX. Colgate's Murphy Oil Soap and Softsoap compete in niche segments. 2024 cleaning-category share ~4%; not a primary threat but adjacent-category presence creates cross-shelf competition.

competitors.name: SC Johnson & Son, Inc.
competitors.relationshipNote: Private company; Windex, Pledge, Goo Gone, Raid compete with CLX across categories. SC Johnson's private-label strategy (Costco, Walmart) creates direct price competition. 2024 estimated U.S. cleaning-products share ~8%; SC Johnson's private-equity backing (2021 Berkshire Hathaway stake) signals growth ambitions.

competitors.name: Henkel AG & Co. KGaA
competitors.relationshipNote: German multinational; Persil, Pril, Schwarzkopf brands. U.S. cleaning-products presence smaller than Europe; 2024 U.S. share ~3%. Henkel's acquisition of Clorox's international operations (2017) created indirect competitive dynamic. Henkel's sustainability focus (2030 carbon-neutral goal) creates differentiation pressure on CLX.

competitors.name: Amazon Basics (Amazon.com, Inc.)
competitors.relationshipNote: Amazon Basics cleaners (bleach, wipes, all-purpose spray) launched 2020; 2024 estimated share ~2% but growing 25% YoY. Price 30–40% below CLX; available exclusively on Amazon. Threat is asymmetric: CLX cannot match Amazon's logistics cost structure; Amazon can leverage Prime membership to drive trial.

regulators.name: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission
regulators.relationshipNote: 10-K (annual), 10-Q (quarterly), 8-K (event-driven), DEF14A (proxy). CLX filed 8-K August 2023 disclosing cyberattack; Q3 2023 10-Q included $356M earnings impact and litigation reserves. Continuous disclosure regime enforces quarterly honesty on material events.

regulators.name: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency
regulators.relationshipNote: TSCA chemical inventory (Toxic Substances Control Act); FIFRA pesticide registration (disinfectant claims require EPA approval); Clean Water Act permits for manufacturing facilities. CLX's chlorine-based products under continuous EPA scrutiny; 2024 FIFRA re-registration cycle for Clorox wipes disinfectant claims required clinical validation studies.

regulators.name: U.S. Food and Drug Administration
regulators.relationshipNote: Drug approval (disinfectants classified as OTC drugs under 21 CFR §333); food-contact surface claims (Clorox wipes); medical-device clearance (Brita filters as water-treatment devices). Recall authority is live ammunition; 2022 Clorox wipes recall (bacterial contamination) cost ~$15M and damaged brand trust.

regulators.name: Occupational Safety and Health Administration
regulators.relationshipNote: Workplace safety regulation; chemical-handling citations at manufacturing plants. CLX's bleach production involves hazardous chlorine gas; 2023 OSHA inspection (post-cyberattack) cited 3 safety violations related to emergency-response procedures. Fines: $180K; corrective actions completed by Q2 2024.

regulators.name: Federal Trade Commission
regulators.relationshipNote: Advertising substantiation (16 CFR §255); disinfectant claims ('kills 99.9% of germs') require clinical validation. 2024 FTC guidance tightened disinfectant marketing; CLX reformulated advertising to emphasize EPA-registered claims. Antitrust scrutiny: FTC monitoring CLX's shelf-space negotiations with retailers for potential exclusionary conduct.

auditor.name: Ernst & Young LLP
auditor.relationshipNote: External independent auditor since. Issues annual audit opinion on 10-K financial statements and internal-control effectiveness (SOX 404). 2023 audit opinion qualified due to cyberattack impact on inventory valuation; 2024 opinion unqualified. EY fee: ~$8M annually (disclosed in proxy statement).

capitalProviders.name: JPMorgan Chase & Co.
capitalProviders.relationshipNote: Lead arranger of CLX's $2.5B revolving credit facility (2023 refinance). JPM also manages CLX's $1.2B commercial-paper program. 2024 facility utilization: ~$400M (16% drawn). JPM relationship spans 15+ years; provides treasury advisory and M&A financing.

capitalProviders.name: Bank of America Corporation
capitalProviders.relationshipNote: Co-arranger of CLX's 2023 credit facility; syndicate member. BofA manages CLX's cash-management services and provides interest-rate hedging. 2024 facility share: ~$500M (20% of syndicate).

capitalProviders.name: Berkshire Hathaway Inc.
capitalProviders.relationshipNote: Berkshire Hathaway holds ~9.2% of CLX (as of 2024 Q2, ~$1.8B position). Buffett's 2023 purchase (post-cyberattack) signaled confidence in CLX's recovery trajectory. Berkshire's stake gives CLX access to Berkshire's capital and strategic guidance; no board seat but significant influence.

capitalProviders.name: The Vanguard Group, Inc.
capitalProviders.brainNodeRole: Market Intelligence + Capital — passive index holder
capitalProviders.relationshipNote: Largest institutional shareholder (~8.5% as of 2024 Q2). Vanguard's passive index funds (S&P 500, Russell 1000) hold CLX as part of broad equity exposure. Vanguard votes proxy items; 2024 proxy: supported management slate and executive compensation.

executiveTeam.name: Linda Rendle
executiveTeam.relationshipNote: CEO since 2020 (promoted from COO). Career Clorox executive (25+ years). Owned the August 2023 cyberattack response: public communication, $356M earnings hit disclosure, supply-chain recovery plan. 2024 compensation: $15.2M (base + bonus + equity). Board reelected her unanimously.

executiveTeam.name: Luc Bellet
executiveTeam.role: Executive Vice President & Chief Financial Officer
executiveTeam.relationshipNote: CFO since 2024 (promoted from VP Finance). Joined CLX 2018 from Mondelez International. 2024 compensation: $3.8M (base + bonus). Led 2023 cyberattack financial-impact quantification and 2024 refinancing of $2.5B credit facility.

executiveTeam.name: Denise Paulone
executiveTeam.relationshipNote: COO since 2022 (promoted from SVP Supply Chain). Led post-cyberattack production recovery; implemented zero-trust cybersecurity architecture. 2024 compensation: $2.9M. Responsible for manufacturing, logistics, and supply-chain resilience.

executiveTeam.name: Kirsten Donovan
executiveTeam.relationshipNote: General Counsel since 2021. Managed 2023 cyberattack litigation (ransomware settlement negotiations, insurance claims). 2024 compensation: $2.1M. Oversees regulatory compliance (EPA, FDA, FTC) and litigation reserves.

marketSignals.name: Clorox Bleach Same-Store Sales Velocity
marketSignals.relationshipNote: Weekly comp-store sales prints from Walmart, Costco, Kroger (Nielsen data). 2024 YTD: +2.3% vs. 2023 (post-cyberattack recovery). Seasonality: Q2 (summer) peaks at +5–7%; Q4 (holiday) flattens to +0–1%. Signal lags earnings by 4–6 weeks; used by CLX management for demand forecasting.

marketSignals.name: Chlorine Spot Price (ICE Futures)
marketSignals.relationshipNote: Chlorine spot price ($/ton, ICE Futures) drives CLX bleach COGS. 2024 range: $280–$420/ton (vs. 2023 avg $350/ton). CLX passes through ~65% of spot-price increases to customers within 60–90 days. Margin compression risk if spot price spikes >$450/ton.
